name: Romie
subcategory: editorial display serif with calligraphic detail
classification_notes: An editorial roman headline serif referencing Lubalin and Bookman with calligraphic flourishes, broad serifs and a generous x-height, placing it in the serif category.
summary: An editorial roman headline serif with broad serifs and calligraphic flourishes, used by brands from Netflix to indie studios.
description: Romie is a headline roman that trades dusty pastiche for a lasting editorial voice, referencing Lubalin in places and Bookman in others, with calligraphic touches throughout. Stable broad serifs, ravishing stroke entasis and a generous x-height run across six weights with italics.
foundry_blurb: Claude Type call Romie an editorial roman headline typeface without the dusty pastiche, giving designers a lasting voice from airy French elegance to long-form New York journalism sensibilities.

name: Kalice
classification_notes: Circular, distinctive serifs drawn from the French Turlot Foundry tradition place Kalice in the serif category, tuned for both headline and text use.
summary: A size-agnostic serif with circular, distinctive serifs drawn from the French Turlot Foundry tradition.
description: Kalice serves headlines, running text and branding equally well, built around circular serifs refined through contemporary tooling for even colour in both print and digital use. Five weights with italics make up Margot Lévêque's second release for the foundry.
foundry_blurb: Claude Type describe Kalice as a lauded sophomore release, its circular and distinctive serifs drawing on the tradition of French Turlot Foundry to achieve fine detail while maintaining even colour.

name: Ninna
classification_notes: Explicitly continuing the pointed-nib, high-contrast tradition of Firmin Didot, Ninna sits firmly in the didone serif category.
summary: A pointed-pen didone headline serif in the Firmin Didot tradition, seen on the Pirelli Calendar.
description: Ninna explores the pointed nib pen through rationally drafted, high-contrast letterforms that continue the conversation started by Firmin Didot. Five weights with italics are built to blend in or stand out across video, print, social and web.
foundry_blurb: Claude Type describe Ninna as a headline typeface in which every letter is a work of art, designed by Margot Lévêque and prepared for every context designers work in.

name: Ernest
subcategory: modern serif with sinuous minuscule serifs
classification_notes: Sinuous, minuscule serifs and broader thin strokes on an otherwise conventional serif skeleton place Ernest in the serif category as a more modern departure for the foundry.
summary: A modern serif debut with sinuous, minuscule serifs, the first Regular cut of a family still in progress.
description: Ernest departs from Claude Type's usual references with sinuous, minuscule serifs and broader thin strokes. Three years in development, its Regular weight launched in 2026 as the first cut of a fuller family still being built out, complete with inventive combining glyphs.
foundry_blurb: Claude Type call Ernest not like their other releases, with sinuous, minuscule serifs and broader thin-strokes walking a more modern, untried path.
